chapter: Retirement and the future of big bands
title: Being billed as the White Duke
summary: Barnet thinks a Variety review coined the label because his stage shows used scrims and production numbers like Ellington's.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Right. Is it true what Leonard reported in the "Book of Jazz," that you were once publicized as the White Duke?
It wasn't anybody's idea that I know of. Somebody -- I don't know who was responsible for it. It certainly wasn't Leonard.
No, he was just reporting it.
But I believe it was probably somebody

that reviewed a show someplace, maybe a Variety -- it sounds like something one of the Variety reviewers might have written, when they review a stage show or something. Because we used to do a lot of the stage mechanics like the Ellington band did. We operated back of a scrim and we had production numbers and things, like Duke used to do. And it was possibly -- I would say it must have been a Variety review that sponsored that thing.
And it sort of hung on for awhile?
Well, anytime you put a label on something, other people pick it up and who knows.
